stem: While applying a back-slab for a child with a fracture, which finding should prompt early referral rather than routine immobilisation and follow-up?

options.text: A distal injury considered for a below-joint slab
Use of a broad plaster roll
Stopping the cast short of joints
Maintaining reduction until the plaster dries

explanation: Neurovascular compromise requires early referral rather than routine immobilisation and follow-up. It is a red flag because compromised blood flow or nerve function needs urgent assessment.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 156

optionExplanations.A: Correct because neurovascular compromise is a red flag that requires early referral and urgent reassessment rather than routine plastering and follow-up.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because distal injuries may be appropriate for a below-joint back-slab when otherwise suitable.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because using a broad plaster roll is part of good plaster technique.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because stopping the cast short of joints is a standard principle of appropriate cast application.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because maintaining reduction until the plaster dries is a key step in successful immobilisation.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
